verdicts.quote: if any row is invalid, or the commit fails, no user exists afterwards (A-2). Visible effects of an import are never partial.
a table of errors (row, column, message) from the response … errors exactly, in order: `(2,email,invalid_email)`, `(3,name,required)`, `(4,email,duplicate_in_file)`, `(6,email,already_exists)`
A row whose email equals an earlier row's in the same file gets `duplicate_in_file` … A row whose email belongs to an existing user gets `already_exists`. Existing users are never modified.
`email,name,role` header with row `a@example.com,A,admin` gives 422 `unknown_column` (column `role`) … role `member` (the product's non-admin default; OG-3)
the endpoint and the page run only for an authenticated user who is an admin at the time of the request
verdicts.missing: The import requires a current admin role. The relationship between that role and permission to create a single user is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: Header: first record; names are trimmed and matched case-insensitively; order is free; exactly the columns `email` and `name` are required and no other column is allowed.
Accepted form: UTF-8 (a leading BOM is ignored), comma-separated, RFC 4180 quoting (double quote doubles to escape, quoted fields may contain commas), CRLF or LF line ends.
a commit failure injected after the second of three inserts gives 500 and the store has 3 users (the fixtures only). … Nothing is emailed by this feature.
S bytes and L rows are accepted; S+1 bytes gives 413; L+1 rows gives 422. … In both, the whole file is rejected and nothing is created.
verdicts.missing: The maximum file size in bytes and maximum number of data rows still need numeric values.

verdicts.quote: a 0-byte file gives 400 `empty_file` … `email,name` alone gives 422 `no_rows` … a file with one row (`solo@example.com,Solo Sam`) gives `total: 1`, `created: 1`
Repeating a successful upload yields 422 with `already_exists` on every row and creates nothing new.
answering with the result report in the same response. … Revisit when OG-6 shows volumes that cannot finish within one request.
verdicts.missing: For files too large to finish in one request, the spec defers both background processing and the way the admin would learn that the job finished.

verdicts.quote: Nothing is emailed by this feature.
Imported users are created in a `pending` state with no password and cannot sign in until activated by a mechanism outside this spec (OG-4).
verdicts.missing: How the user activates the account, obtains credentials and signs in for the first time remains open.

verdicts.quote: Uploaded file bytes: held in request memory only; never written to disk or the datastore, deleted when the request ends
`importId`, admin id, UTC timestamp, sanitised original file name (no path, at most 255 characters), `total`, `created`, outcome (`completed`, `rejected`, `failed`).
Recovery: nothing to repair after failure; the admin fixes the file and re-uploads.
verdicts.missing: The spec gives a whole-file retry. It leaves cancellation during processing unspecified and provides no way to retry only failed rows.

verdicts.quote: Upload disabled, a progress indicator, a polite live-region message "Uploading" … The bound on response time at L rows **is unresolved** (missing decision: L and an acceptable duration).
verdicts.missing: The maximum completion time at the supported limit is undecided. The indicator is specified for uploading, with no measure of server-side processing progress.

verdicts.quote: Existing users are never modified.
verdicts.missing: The spec does not require the existing manual single-user creation flow to keep its current behavior.

verdicts.quote: name of exactly 100 characters passes, 101 fails; email of exactly 254 characters passes, 255 fails … no error-report download … Spreadsheet-formula neutralisation matters on any future export and is out of scope here.
